methods.name: GARCH(p, q) by conditional maximum likelihood with normal or standardised Student-t errors; inverse-observed-information SEs; variance forecasts
methods.reference: conditional GARCH(p, q) likelihood written out in R (fGarch and rugarch not installed): fGarch's mci start h_t = mean(e^2) for t <= max(p, q) and its standardised t; maximised by optim, then Newton iterations on the analytic gradient; SEs sqrt(diag(-H^-1)) with H from numDeriv::jacobian of the analytic gradient; forecasts by the GARCH recursion; tseries::garch likelihood identity on the demeaned series
quantities: parameter on the alpha2 = 0 bound (restricted maximum, SEs of the free parameters)
printed coefficient table (row names and SEs)
methods.tolerance: iterative MLE with a finite-difference Hessian, looser than validation/README.md's n > 1000 row: parameters, h_t and forecasts 1e-8 relative (bound fit 1e-6), SEs, z and covariances 1e-6 relative, p-values 1e-5 relative + 1e-12 absolute, logLik/AIC/BIC 1e-8 relative (Tol::stat); Appendix A.31 optim keys as cross-checks at 1e-5
